name: A pair reserves two values
why: No singleton exists. Pairwise AC leaves x2 with three values; global support removes v0 and v1.

name: Three tasks, only two slots
why: Every binary disequality has support, but a Hall deficiency rules out all injective assignments.

name: An augmenting reassignment
why: A greedy x0=v0 would strand x1; exact matching instead reassigns x0 to v1.

name: Two interchangeable assignments
why: All four edges have a full assignment witness. A chosen matching is not the only solution.

name: Surplus value is allowed
why: Distinct does not mean surjective. Unused values remain legal.

name: An empty domain
why: An empty domain certifies failure immediately. Synchronous binary propagation can then empty other domains.

name: Empty scope, one empty tuple
why: The empty assignment satisfies the empty all-different constraint; count is one, maximum size is zero.

name: Singleton cascade
why: Full synchronous pairwise rounds show ordinary binary propagation is not deliberately stopped early.

name: A noninterval Hall set
why: Holes matter: x0 and x1 reserve {v0,v2}, so x2 can only use v1. No bounds-only claim.

name: Maximum supported family
why: Six variables each allow eight values: 20,160 complete injective assignments; all 48 edges supported.
